subject: NA prevalences and single base pair segments

messages.author: af46f37e5a5fa00d
messages.subject: NA prevalences and single base pair segments
parts:
I'm using the TITANRunner pipeline on WES data, and I noticed a couple of odd things in the output *_segs.txt files. There are some segments where the Clonal_Cluster and Clonal_Frequency columns are both NA and the copy number is 2, for example

tumour 2 179300971 179315757 14787 0.74 0.03 3 HET 2 1 1 NA NA

Also, there are some segments which appear to be a single base pair in length,

tumour 2 113589075 113589075 1 0.83 -1.14 1 DLOH 1 0 1 1 1.00

Currently, I'm assuming the NA's mean that every cell in the sample is in that copy number/LOH state and am setting the prevalence to 1 in those cases. I'm also discarding the single base pair segments. Do these actions make sense?

Thanks for answering all my questions!

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: NA prevalences and single base pair segments
parts:
Hi Rosemary,

Thanks for your question.

For copy number of 2 and heterozygous status, the cellular prevalence and clonal cluster is set to NA by design.  Only copy number alterations (<2 or >2) and non-heterozygous status will have a clonal assignment.  When a locus has a normal genotype (neutral and heterozygous) it is less relevant to refer to its clonality.  On the other hand, cancer-specific tumour genotypes will have a (sub)clonal assignment because these are events of interest for which we are trying to determine clonality.

Single position segments can arise due to noisy outliers.  Particularly, in your WES data, neighboring SNPs may be more distant and the HMM will tend to segment (transition) for longer inter-SNP distances.  You can do try a few things to reduce these segments:

1) Increase self-transition probabilities by setting these arguments in "runEMclonalCN"
txnZstrength and txnExpLen
These can also be set in the config.cfg file for TITANRunner

2) Post-process the results by removing these outliers.

Hope this helps,
Gavin

messages.author: af46f37e5a5fa00d
messages.subject: Re: NA prevalences and single base pair segments
parts: Thanks for the clarification Gavin. The rest of the segments look pretty good so I'm inclined to just remove the outliers with post-processing.
